mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever wondered why some stories seem to fill every headline, while others barely get a mention? Welcome—let's set out together on a journey to uncover the forces that quietly shape what we see, hear, and believe. Drawing inspiration from Edward S. Herman's eye-opening work, Manufacturing Consent: The Political Economy of the Mass Media, we'll explore how media institutions, political power, and economic interests all intertwine behind the scenes. It's fascinating—and a little unsettling—to realize the ways news is filtered and framed, not just reported. As we dig into the hidden patterns—why certain voices are lifted up while others are pushed aside—you'll start to see how public opinion is shaped, sometimes without us even noticing. Together, we'll peel back the layers on ownership, advertising, sourcing, and more, revealing how these structures quietly guide what becomes news and what fades into the background. It's not just about the media—it's about the health of our democracy and our role as engaged citizens. So, as we step into this world of curated information, let's keep our curiosity sharp and our minds open. Get ready to rethink what it means to be truly informed—and why that matters more than ever.
